title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
subtitle: Moist loaf cake with a sharp lemon syrup crust
excerpt: A moist, buttery loaf cake soaked while hot with a sharp lemon sugar syrup that sets into a thin, crackly crust. One of Britain's most beloved cakes. The drizzle is not a glaze: it should soak in.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lemon drizzle cake became one of Britain's most popular home-baked cakes during the 1970s and 1980s and has remained at or near the top of national cake surveys ever since. The recipe is a simple all-in-one Victoria sponge mixture with lemon zest, baked in a loaf tin and finished with a lemon and sugar drizzle poured over while still hot. The drizzle soaks in as the cake cools, creating a moist crumb and a crisp, sugary crust.

content.text: The drizzle must go on while the cake is still hot in the tin: this allows the syrup to soak in rather than sit on top. Prick the surface all over with a skewer before pouring. The sugar will not dissolve completely: that is correct, and the undissolved crystals form the crackly crust.

items.preparation: zest of both, juice of one for the batter

content.text: Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, lemon zest, lemon juice, and milk until just combined.
Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.

Mix the icing sugar with the juice of the remaining lemon. While the cake is still hot in the tin, prick all over with a skewer. Pour the drizzle slowly over the top. Leave to cool completely in the tin before turning out.
